pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all seeded rows are 0 and that value 2 is rejected.
'AC-2' test asserts exact list with ★ only on the starred item.
'AC-3' test stars 3 and 1 and asserts only those, in id order, status 200.
'AC-4' test checks / and /?show=all give the full list in id order.

The link behaviour is implemented (VIEWS links in src/index.js) and a test checks it, but the last commit f5609ee renamed that test from 'AC-5: each view links to the other' to 'each view links to the other'. No test names AC-5 now, and the spec doesn't mark it 'verified by review'.
'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__; Object.hasOwn guards the lookup.

findings.what: Commit f5609ee ('Follow-up edits') removed the 'AC-5:' prefix from the link test's title. AC-5 is no longer named by any test, so it is unmet under the naming rule. The change was made after the go, with no recorded decision, and the PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing'.
findings.fix: Restore the title 'AC-5: each view links to the other'.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing' and that test/starred.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-7. The last commit changed the test that covered AC-5 and stripped its AC id, so both claims are false.
findings.fix: Restore the AC-5 test name, or state the change honestly in the PR.

findings.what: The link test only checks the full list and the non-empty starred view. The empty-state tests check only for 'Starred only' or 'All items', not the href.
findings.fix: Optional: assert the full anchor in the state tests.

lenses.note: The spec exists. All items are implemented, and the scope matches except for the disclosed traffic-check script change, which is needed to carry the query route.
AC-5 is unnamed by any test after the last commit. All four state-table rows have tests.
The tests assert behaviour. The traffic fake app was extended, not loosened.
The README mentions ?show=starred, which matches the code.
No defects found. Object.hasOwn guards the view lookup and the SQL is static.
The show value is whitelisted, titles are escaped, and the SQL has no user input. No planted instructions were found.
The diff touches no UI files beyond a minimal server-rendered HTML page, and the spec has no design requirements.
No browser flow or screenshots exist, and the PR says 'Preview: none'.
The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false (see the finding). The title is under 72 characters.
